This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual/ Physical Mode).
2.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner as well as learned counsel for the informant and learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State-Opposite Party.
Perused the application as well as documents annexed thereto.

3. The present application has been filed invoking the inherent powers of this court under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. with a prayer to quash the criminal proceeding/F.I.R. arising out of Khordha Model P.S. Case No.176 of 2024 corresponding to G.R. Case No.422 of 2024 for alleged commission of offence under Sections 498A, 323, 294, 506, 34 I.P.C. read with Section 4 of D.P. Act pending in the file of learned S.D.J.M., Khordha.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners at the outset submitted that the petitioner No.1 is the husband and the Opposite Party No.2 is the wife.
He further contended that there exists a matrimonial dispute between the Petitioner No.1 and Opposite Party No.2.

Learned counsel for the petitioners further contended that as a result of the aforesaid matrimonial dispute the present criminal case has been registered at the instance of the Opposite Party No.2 against the Petitioner No.1-husband and ) Akash Mishra vs ) State Of Odisha .....

the Petitioner No.2 -mother-in-law of the informant
. He further contended that in the meantime the matter has been amicably settled between the parties by the intervention of the well-wishers of the parties and family members.
As a result, both the petitioner No.1 and Opposite Party No.2 have come to a conclusion that they want to settle the matter amicably on compromise.

On such grounds,
learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that any further continuance of the proceeding would be an abuse the process of law.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the Opposite Party No.2 supports the contention of the learned counsel for the Petitioner No.1 to the extent that the matter has been amicably settled between the parties.

He further contended that the compromise which has been arrived at between the parties has been reduced into writing in the shape of an agreement dated 22.05.2024.
6.
On perusal of the said agreement, it appears that both the Petitioner No.1 as well as the Opposite Party No.2 have agreed to resolve the dispute amicably.
As a result of the aforesaid settlements the parties have agreed to part ways gracefully and have decided to live peacefully.
The agreement further reveals that a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- has been paid to the Opposite Party No.2 by the Petitioner No.1.

Further, the agreement reveals that the parties have agreed to go for a divorce before the learned Family Judge, Khordha and both have agreed to cooperate with each other for obtaining a mutual divorce decree.

7. Additionally, in the course of hearing today both the Petitioner No.1 as well as Opposite Party No.2 filed two separate affidavits, wherein the receipt of the payment of sum of Rs.1,50,000/- has been acknowledged by the Opposite Party No.2 and both have stated that the matter has been settled on compromise.
Furthermore, the Opposite Party No.2 has stated that she has no objection in the event the proceeding is quashed by this Court.
Both affidavits are taken on record.

8. Taking into consideration the fact that the present case arises out of a matrimonial dispute and the fact that the parties have decided to resolve the matter amicably through a settlement which has been reduced to writing in the shape of an agreement dated 22.05.2024, the further continuance of the proceeding would be an abuse of process of law.

Further, keeping in view the terms and conditions of the agreement dated 22.05.2024, this Court is of the view that it would be in the larger interest of justice to quash the pending criminal proceeding against the present petitioner.

Accordingly, Khordha Model P.S. Case No.176 of 2024 corresponding to G.R. Case No.422 of 2024 is hereby quashed subject to the terms and conditions as has been agreed upon by the parties vide agreement dated 22.05.2024 under Annexure-2 to the petition.
9.
